{{Current events|year=2021|month=03|day=13|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[car bomb]]ing near a [[police station]] in [[Herat Province]] kills at least eight people and wounds more than 50 others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/13/car-bomb-in-afghanistans-herat-province-kills-several (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Twelve people are killed after [[Myanmar Army|soldiers]] open fire on protesters in [[Mandalay]], [[Yangon]], and [[Pyay]]. A 13-year-old child is among those killed, the youngest victim of the unrest to date. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN2B503Q (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*''[[Avatar (2009 film)|Avatar]]'' retakes its place as the world's [[List of highest-grossing films|highest-grossing film]] of all time from ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'' following a domestic release in [[China]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/03/13/avatar-once-again-highest-grossing-film-of-all-time-at-the-box-office.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''

*A [[Armed Forces of the Republic of Kazakhstan|Kazakh Air Force]] [[Antonov An-26]] crashes in [[Almaty]], killing four crew members on board and wounding two others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kazakhstan-airplane-crash/kazakh-military-plane-crash-in-almaty-kills-four-idUSKBN2B50CV?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reaches a milestone of five million people having received their first [[vaccination]] shot. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-france-idUKKBN2B50N8 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (country)]]
****[[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] receives 43,200 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] distributed through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://agenda.ge/en/news/2021/670 (Agenda)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports a record 9,444 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 507,627. [https://hungarytoday.hu/hungary-coronavirus-new-record-cases-saturday/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wales]]
*****[[Wales]] begins to ease their first step of [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions, with "[[Stay-at-home order|stay-at-home]]" replaced by "stay local". According to new rules, four people from two households can meet outside and outdoor sports can be resumed. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/03/13/wales-lockdown-rules-when-restrictions-end-review-covid-travel/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]]
****[[Jordan]]'s health minister resigns after six [[COVID-19]] patients die due to a lack of supplemental [[oxygen]] at a hospital ward in [[Al-Salt]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-56381870 (BBC News)]
****Jordan receives 144,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] distributed through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://en.royanews.tv/news/26165/2021-03-13 (Roya News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 169 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,833. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-03/13/c_139807549.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a person who travelled from [[Brazil]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1406476/doh-confirms-phs-first-case-of-covid-19-brazil-variant (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia]]
****[[Ethiopia]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19 in order to reduce the number of COVID-19 infections, a week after the country received 2.2 million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/ethiopia-begins-covid-19-vaccine-rollout/2174904 (Anadolu Agency)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. Health workers, soldiers, people over age 65, and people with underlying conditions are the first to receive the vaccine. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/tunisia-starts-vaccination-campaign-sputnik-shots-76434678 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[PlainSite]] public data reveal 450 workers at the [[Tesla Fremont Factory|Tesla Factory]] in [[Fremont, California|Fremont]] have tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] since [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Elon Musk]] reopened the building last May. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/13/world/tesla-elon-musk-coronavirus-outbreak.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Australia]] reports its first local [[COVID-19]] cases in two weeks, when a doctor in [[Brisbane]] tests positive. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/australasia/australia-covid-cases-brisbane-uk-variant-b1816759.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***Former [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] receives his first dose of the [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210313-brazil-s-lula-receives-first-dose-of-coronavirus-vaccine (France 24)]
***[[Legislative Assembly of Mato Grosso]] member [[Silvio Favero]], known for introducing a bill against mandatory COVID-19 vaccinations, dies from COVID-19 in [[Cuiabá]], Brazil. [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2021/03/15/brazilian-anti-vax-politician-has-died-from-covid-19/ (Euro Weekly News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]], [[Hong Kong protests (2019-present)|Hong Kong protests]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] formally declares [[China]] to be in breach of the 1984 [[Sino-British Joint Declaration]], saying that China is now in "a state of ongoing non-compliance" of the treaty. [[Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom|Foreign Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]] says that the UK will "continue to stand up for the people of Hong Kong". [https://www.ft.com/content/dc2aaf68-b92e-4c48-8823-e7e4648ccb74 (''Financial Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death of Sarah Everard]]
**A [[Metropolitan Police]] officer is [[remanded in custody]] and will appear at the [[Old Bailey]] in [[London]] on March 16. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-56385657 (BBC)]
**At a candlelight [[vigil]] in [[Clapham]], mourners defying COVID-19 gathering restrictions clash with police officers attempting to disperse them, resulting in four arrests. The actions of the police draw condemnation from several officials, including [[Mayor of London|London Mayor]] [[Sadiq Khan]] and [[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]]. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/sarah-everard-vigil-defy-police-ban-clapham-common-b923959.html (''Evening Standard'')]
*[[2020–21 United States racial unrest]], [[Shooting of Breonna Taylor]]
**People rally in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], on the first anniversary of the shooting death of Breonna Taylor. Ms. Taylor was shot by officers who forced entry to her home using a "no-knock" warrant which meant they did not announce themselves. Surrounding roads are closed off, but many felt the security measures were excessive. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-56387446 (BBC)]
*[[2019 Bolivian political crisis]]
**Former interim [[President of Bolivia|President]] [[Jeanine Áñez]] is arrested by [[law enforcement in Bolivia|police]] and is accused of participating in an alleged [[coup d'état]] against ousted President [[Evo Morales]] in November 2019. Before being arrested, Áñez denounced the arrest and stated that the "persecution had begun". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-56381697 (BBC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Western Australian state election]]
**The [[Australian Labor Party (Western Australia Branch)|Labor Party]] wins the state election in [[Western Australia]], in one of the biggest landslide victories in the country's history. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-03-13/wa-election-winner-called-in-state-election-2021-by-antony-green/13243662 (ABC Australia)]
